encoder: a single Sonnet 5.5 agent working alone from the brief in BRIEF.md
display_name: Misrepresentation Act 1967 (Singapore), whole Act, two layers (the law, and a seat layer), target main
seat: a person who entered into a contract after a false statement was made to them, asking on facts they can state whether they may claim damages or rescind, and whether the other party's clause excluding that liability works
edition: Misrepresentation Act 1967 (Singapore), 2020 Revised Edition, informal consolidation, plain-text rendering of the Singapore Statutes Online text retrieved 2026-10-01 (not the official text)
scope: Encoded: ss 1, 2(1), 2(2), 2(3), 3 and 4 in full, as decision rules (s 2(2) also as a regulative MAY rule), with the Interpretation Act 1965 s 2(1) words "person", "party" and "court" looked up in the copied table. Inert: the title page, long title, headings, date line, arrangement of sections, page furniture, Legislative History and abbreviations (not operative); s 5, the short title (machinery). The Act defines no term. Taken as inputs, not encoded: the general-law right to rescind, the law of deceit, Unfair Contract Terms Act 1977 s 11(1), Civil Law Act 1909 s 5, every court judgment.
not_reviewed: No domain expert has read this encoding against the text. The forks F1 to F13 and the section "Marginal readings for a lawyer" in NOTES.md are for a lawyer to rule on.

dependencies.note: the blob is the file as it stands in Commons; the copy carries a 3-line header, copied unchanged on 2026-11-05
dependencies.used: Interpretation Act 1965 s 2(1): "person" and "party" (entry 59), "court" (entry 22), in ma-reading.l4

inputs_not_staged: Civil Law Act 1909 s 5 (as in force before 12 November 1993)

checks.note: check.sh, target main, run with both main builds; first run, no earlier baseline. A DEONTIC value cannot be asserted on main: the s 2(2) permission is traced (4 traces, identical on 1.6.109 and 1.6.108) and the same permission is a decision rule that is asserted.
checks.quotes: python3 -I check-quotes.py: every quotation of the Act's words (and of the copied Interpretation Act's words) in a FALSE-kind or NOTHING-kind comment is a slice of its source; four single words quoted as words the text does not use, and the pointers to "Reading a result", are allow-listed by name
checks.coverage: python3 -I coverage.py: every non-blank line of the text is in a row
